title: USACE example E-2 (fig. E-10), ponded water

meta.title: USACE example E-2 (fig. E-10), ponded water
meta.notes: Undrained three-layer slope with 8 ft of water ponded against its toe (pool el. 0), on a commercial program's circle (48.262, 28, R = 47.683 ft; Fig. 68.2). Converted to SI.

source.reference: USACE EM 1110-2-1902 (2003), appendix E, example E-2, fig. E-10.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V091 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: The text describes USACE's circle (center 8.4 ft right of and 36 ft above the toe, tangent to the base of soil 3: 48.4, 28, R = 48); commercial program A's printed circle is slightly smaller. cSlope gives the same FOS on both (1.235).

The water above the toe acts as a load on the ground surface. The manual's chart value for this circle is 1.24 (p. E-20: c_avg 499 psf, μw 0.95, Pd 2253, N0 5.6); an earlier entry gave 1.33, which does not occur in the manual for this example (checked against docs/kallor/usace-em-1110-2-1902.md, 2026-10-25).

With φ = 0 in every layer the moment equilibrium about the center does not depend on the interslice forces, so Bishop, Spencer and Morgenstern-Price coincide on a circle (cSlope 1.2348, 1.2348, 1.2349); commercial program A's GLE 1.244 lies 0.24 % above its own Bishop and Spencer 1.241.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
agua embalsada: la piezométrica pasa sobre el terreno; ogs la incluye en todas las versiones, con su peso y su empuje horizontal y sin sismo (F5.3); cSlope la carga con `followBoundary: false`.
